name: Unauthorized Message
summary: Adversaries may send unauthorized messages to ICS systems and devices to evade defenses or manipulate processes. Unauthorized messages can be categorized as either reporting messages that contain telemetry data about the current state of systems, devices, and processes or as command messages which instruct systems and devices on how to operate. By injecting unauthorized messages, adversaries can make it appear as if everything is working…

analytics.name: Analytic 2045
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies an Industrial Control System (ICS) protocol message arriving at a device from a source whose identity is not in the approved communication baseline for that destination, where the message is structurally valid but originates outside the documented set of legitimate communicators. This technique-level analytic synthesizes Command Message (T1692.001) and Reporting Message (T1692.002). OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry…

analytics.name: Analytic 2160
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies an Industrial Control System (ICS) protocol library loaded by a Linux process not in the authorized ICS applications list, making connections to the device subnet. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures.

log_sources.channel: IPFIX/NetFlow flow record (src/dst IP, src/dst port, protocol, packets/bytes/time): first-seen connection from a source to an Industrial Control System (ICS) device outside the documented approved communication matrix
